name: MathlibAnnex.Topology.exists_isOpen_singleton
title: An isolated point in a countable Baire space

content.display_title: An isolated point in a countable Baire space
content.one_sentence_role: Applies the Baire property to the closed cover by singletons.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $X$ be a nonempty countable topological space which is $T_1$ and Baire. Then some point $x\in X$ is isolated: its singleton $\{x\}$ is open.
content.assumptions: The $T_1$ condition says that singletons are closed. No metric, completeness, compactness or Hausdorff assumption beyond $T_1$ is required.
content.conclusion: At least one singleton is open; the conclusion does not say that every point is isolated.
content.proof_summary: A countable closed cover of a nonempty Baire space has a member with nonempty interior.
proof_steps: The $T_1$ property makes each $F_x=\{x\}$ closed. Since $X$ is countable, $$X=\bigcup_{x\in X}F_x$$ is a countable closed cover. The [Closed-cover Baire theorem with the singleton family](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Topology/CountableBaire.lean#L18-L28) applies because $X$ is nonempty and Baire.

It yields $x$ with $\operatorname{int}(F_x)\ne\varnothing$. Choose $y$ in that interior. Since $\operatorname{int}(F_x)\subseteq\{x\}$, $y=x$, so $x\in\operatorname{int}\{x\}$. Thus $$\{x\}\subseteq\operatorname{int}\{x\}\subseteq\{x\},$$ and $\{x\}$ equals its interior and is open.
